item.problem_statement: An emulated protocol has to fix three times that a randomized trial fixes in one act, when eligibility is assessed, when treatment is assigned, and when follow-up begins, and it has to fix the resolution at which time is measured, because routine data arrive as dated records rather than as scheduled visits. Clone-censor-weight and sequential emulation handle the misalignment; neither chooses the grace period or the interval width, and estimates move with both. A coarse interval lets treatment affect an outcome inside the interval before censoring applies; a fine interval produces high-dimensional nuisance models and unstable weights. Selection tools exist and use outcome information: cross-validated variance has been evaluated as a measure of data support for choosing a discretization. The described reporting instead illustrates why a target-trial label or checklist cannot itself establish the full assumption burden.

item.problem_title: Calling an analysis a target trial emulation is treated as evidence about its assumption burden
item.problem_statement: Target trial specification improves temporal alignment, protocol clarity and estimand definition. It does not establish consistency, conditional exchangeability, positivity, valid measurement, correct estimation or transportability, and those are separate conditions rather than steps on one scale: any of them can hold while the others fail. In practice the label does the work of all of them. An analysis that adopts the framework is read as though the whole set had been secured, and no convention asks a study to state the six requirements separately for the estimand it chose. The reporting evidence shows how weakly the label constrains the practice: of 200 published studies claiming to emulate a trial, 43% did not describe all key emulation components.

item.problem_title: Transporting an observational estimate compounds sampling assumptions on top of confounding assumptions with no accounting
item.problem_statement: An internally valid estimate need not apply to the health system, population or calendar period where the decision will be made. Transporting an observational contrast requires treatment exchangeability in the source, effect exchangeability across samples conditional on a sufficient measured set, and positivity for both treatment and sampling. A sufficient set is weaker than every effect modifier: modifiers that do not differ across populations or that are irrelevant after conditioning need not be observed. Transport estimators are now being applied to emulations, including post hoc standardization of emulations to their trial populations inside a benchmarking program. What remains is the accounting. item.problem_title: No estimator is defensible as a default, and no study is required to show that its choice mattered
item.problem_statement: The available estimators differ in what they assume rather than only in how they perform. Active-comparator new-user designs with regression or propensity adjustment handle baseline initiation and not treatment-confounder feedback. Matching gives a transparent population, discards information, and often leaves its estimand unstated. Marginal structural models represent regime effects directly and are unstable under extreme weights. The parametric g-formula supports flexible estimands and is sensitive to sequential outcome-model misspecification. G-estimation avoids modeling the treatment-free outcome distribution and is technically demanding. Longitudinal targeted learning is doubly robust, computationally heavy and sensitive to practical positivity. No estimator is defensible as a universal default, and a study reporting one reports a number whose dependence on that choice is unknown: n

item.evidence: This is the comparison the entry says nothing requires: five approaches on one question, with a plasmode simulation giving a known truth. It establishes the entry's premise quantitatively, since the estimates range from 0.54 to 0.88 in the same data and three methods that are all unbiased in simulation still disagree. It addresses one question in one database, so it does not supply the common benchmark or the synthesis the entry asks for.

item.evidence: This supplies a formal treatment of competing events for a case the existing framework did not cover, mediation with a nonseparable exposure and a nonterminal mediator, by making the competing pathway an explicit part of the estimand rather than a censoring rule. It also reports a survival probability difference rather than a hazard difference on the grounds of causal interpretability. It does not cover recurrent events under sustained strategies, which the authors name as future work.
item.quote: Formal definitions and considerations for causal effects in the presence of competing risks have been published, but not for the mediation analysis setting when the exposure is not separable and both the outcome and the mediator are nonterminal events.
